questions.stem:
Consider the following code segment.

```text
nums ← [8, 6, 10, 1, 12, 12]
evens ← []
FOR EACH n IN nums
{
   IF (n MOD 2 = 0)
   {
      APPEND(evens, n)
   }
}
DISPLAY (LENGTH(evens))
```

What is displayed as a result of running the code segment?

options.why: Recheck each element.
Correct. Apply the condition to every element of the list.
Even numbers have remainder 0.
LENGTH counts elements; it does not add them.

questions.explanation: 5 values are even.

questions.stem:
The procedure `substring(str, start, length)` returns `length` characters of `str` beginning at position `start`; the first character is at position 1. The procedure `concat(a, b)` returns `a` joined to `b`. What is displayed?

```text
word ← "keyboard"
other ← "internet"
DISPLAY (concat(substring(word, 2, 4), substring(other, 7, 2)))
```

options.why: The first character is at position 1, not 0.
concat joins its arguments in the order given.
Correct. Positions start at 1 in AP pseudocode.
length is 4, so 4 characters are taken.

questions.explanation: substring("keyboard", 2, 4) is "eybo" and substring("internet", 7, 2) is "et", so the result is "eyboet".

questions.stem: A procedure `countAbove(list)` should return how many values in list are greater than 14, but the programmer suspects it uses ≥ instead of >. Which test input would reveal this error?

options.why: No value is 14 or above, so both versions return 0.
No value equals 14, so both versions agree.
Every value is above 14, so both versions return the same count.

questions.explanation: Only an input containing the boundary value 14 makes ≥ and > behave differently.

questions.stem: A network has computers P, Q, R, S, T, U. The direct connections are: P–S, P–T, P–U, Q–R, Q–S, Q–U, R–S, R–T. What is the minimum number of connections that must fail for computer P to be unable to communicate with computer U?

options.why: After that many failures a path still remains.
Correct. Removing 2 well-chosen connections separates P from U; removing fewer always leaves a path.
Some set of 2 connections already disconnects them.
Not every connection needs to fail.

questions.explanation: P has 3 connections and U has 2. Checking failures systematically shows that 2 is the fewest that leaves no path between them.

parts.prompt: (Algorithm development) Explain in detailed steps how the algorithm in `longestStreak` uses sequencing, selection and iteration to produce its result.
